notes: The MKR 1000 WiFi is not in the catalogue, so a new part type arduino-mkr-1000 was created, with ports taken from the pin labels in the diagram.

The breadboard half with rows f-j is treated as bank 'b'. Columns were read from the image: green wire at column 3, resistor from column 3 to column 6, LED legs in columns 6 and 8, black wire in column 8.
The LED leg with the bend (column 6) is taken as the anode. This matches the schematic, where pin 2 goes through the resistor to the LED anode and the cathode goes to GND.
The tutorial calls for a USB cable to power and program the board, but it is not shown in the diagrams, so it is not included.
The sketch uses LED_BUILTIN and reads A1, but the external LED is on pin 2 according to the diagram and text. Nothing is connected to A1.
The text says 'Jumper wires'. Both wires in the diagram are drawn as jumpers, so they are modelled as jumper-wire.
